title: What the ZPA Terraform provider does when deleting objects with dependents
aliases: detach from policy rules on delete

prose.text: Before deleting a PRA portal, PRA console, segment group or server group, it walks the objects that reference it and rewrites them. The outcome depends on how each of those cleanups handles failure, and they differ.

console-is-its-own-resource.conditions: The absence of any ownership or state check in detachAndCleanUpPRAPortals rests on reading that function in full at v4.4.10 and at the pin; it is not a quotable fact.

portal-delete-can-delete-console.statement: So deleting a portal that is the only portal of a console also deletes that console, including a console Terraform manages as its own resource (in another configuration or state, or when the portal is removed or targeted alone). On the next refresh that console drops out of state and the plan recreates it.
portal-delete-can-delete-console.conditions: Applies when the portal is listed as the sole portal of at least one console. Whether the API itself requires a console to keep at least one portal (which is the likely reason for the provider's choice) is gap api-console-without-portals.

server-group-cleanup-failures-only-logge.statement: Every failure inside the three server-group cleanups is logged and dropped: listing or updating policy rules, listing or updating application segments, and fetching or updating individual connector groups. The connector-group helper returns nil after its loop whatever happened there; only a failure to fetch the server group itself returns an error, and the caller logs and ignores that too.

server-group-delete-can-succeed-with-ref.statement: So a server-group destroy can finish successfully in Terraform while policy rules, application segments or connector groups still reference the deleted group, with the only trace in the provider's debug log.
server-group-delete-can-succeed-with-ref.conditions: Depends on a cleanup write failing and on the ZPA API then accepting deletion of a group that is still referenced (gap api-delete-referenced-object). If the API rejects such a delete, Terraform reports that error instead.

cleanups-can-leave-partial-detach.statement: A failed segment-group, PRA portal or PRA console destroy can leave the object detached from some rules or consoles and still attached to others. A retry starts from that partially changed state and is not equivalent to one atomic operation.
cleanups-can-leave-partial-detach.conditions: Follows from sequential writes with no rollback; the quoted code shows no rollback or batching, established by reading each cleanup function in full at v4.4.10 and the pin. Assumes each earlier write took effect on the server.

portal-deleted-console-skips-policy-deta.statement: A console deleted by the portal cleanup is deleted with a direct API call, not through the console resource's delete, so the credential-policy detach that the console resource runs first is skipped.
portal-deleted-console-skips-policy-deta.conditions: The portal cleanup function, read in full at v4.4.10 and the pin, calls the console delete directly and never calls the console's policy detach. What the API does with credential-policy rules that still reference a deleted console is gap api-delete-referenced-object.

api-console-without-portals.title: Whether the ZPA API allows a PRA console with no portals
api-console-without-portals.blocks: knowing whether deleting the emptied console is required by the API or a provider choice
api-console-without-portals.detail: No captured source states whether a console may exist with an empty portal list. Test in a scratch tenant by updating a console to an empty portal list and observing the response.

api-delete-referenced-object.title: What the ZPA API does when deleting a server group that is still referenced
api-delete-referenced-object.blocks: stating whether a failed provider cleanup surfaces as a delete error or as silent dangling references
api-delete-referenced-object.detail: The provider assumes it must detach references before deleting. No captured source states whether the API rejects deleting a referenced server group or removes the references itself. Test in a scratch tenant by deleting a server group still used by a rule and a segment, then re-reading both. Unverified legacy statement (operator observation): a server group with ipAnchored true could not be deleted while referenced, and setting ipAnchored to false first was the workaround.
